depth.h2: What Elgin Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: Elgin’s homes span more than 150 years. About 1 in 5 were built before 1940, and nearly 3 in 10 went up between 1990 and 2009. Add the Fox River and heavy summer storms, and each part of town has its own plumbing problems.

tiles.title: Historic Homes Near Downtown
tiles.body: The Elgin Historic District, the oldest part of the city, has nearly 700 buildings, many from the 1800s. Homes from that era often still run on cast iron drains, galvanized water lines and clay sewer pipe. Galvanized pipe rusts from the inside and slowly cuts water pressure, and clay pipe cracks and lets roots in. A [camera inspection](/elgin/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows the condition of your line before you decide on a [sewer repair](/elgin/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: Summer Storms and Flooded Basements
tiles.body: In July 2017, more than 7 inches of rain fell just south of Elgin in two days, and basements flooded across the area. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/elgin/sump-pumps) keeps running when the power goes out. A [backflow valve](/elgin/flood-control-maintenance) stops sewage from coming up through floor drains. If you’ve already had [water in the basement](/elgin/basement-flooding), we can help you find where it came from.

tiles.title: Newer West Side Homes, Original Equipment
tiles.body: Nearly 3 in 10 Elgin homes went up between 1990 and 2009. Equipment that came with the house, like the first water heater and the first sump pump, isn’t built to last 20 or 30 years. A [water heater that leaks or runs out too fast](/elgin/water-heater-repair) is usually the first to go. A [whole-home checkup](/elgin/plumbing-maintenance) tells you what’s close to the end before it fails.

tiles.title: Winter Freezes and Hidden Leaks
tiles.body: Fox Valley winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and a split pipe often starts leaking inside a wall once it thaws. Water stains on a ceiling or a meter that moves when nothing is running are the signs to watch for. We can [find and fix the leak](/elgin/leak-repairs), and we’re on call 24/7 if a [pipe bursts](/elgin/burst-pipe-repair).

items.q: My home near downtown Elgin is over 100 years old. What should I check?
items.preview: Start with the sewer line and the water lines.
items.a: Start with the sewer line and the water lines. Homes from that era often have clay sewer pipe, cast iron drains and galvanized water pipe, and all of them wear out with age. A camera inspection shows the condition of your sewer line, and low water pressure is often a sign that galvanized pipe is closing up inside. Age alone doesn’t mean something is wrong, but an inspection lets you plan repairs instead of reacting to a leak.

items.q: Why does my kitchen drain keep clogging?
items.a: Grease is the usual cause. It goes down the drain as a liquid, cools and sticks to the pipe walls, and food scraps get caught in it. Over time the opening narrows until water barely moves. A plunger or a store-bought cleaner might help for a while, but [professional drain cleaning](/elgin/drain-cleaning) clears the buildup from the pipe walls so the clog doesn’t come right back.

items.q: When should I replace my water heater?
items.preview: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years.
items.a: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Rusty water, rumbling noises, a leak at the base or hot water that runs out faster than it used to all mean it’s time to have it checked. [Replacing it](/elgin/water-heater-installation) on your schedule is easier than dealing with a flooded basement.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from sewer backups?
items.preview: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris.
items.a: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris. For homes with repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/elgin/overhead-sewer-systems) lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen. We can look at your setup and tell you which option makes sense for your home.
